topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The opening frames the lecture on cancer causation and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Mutations, susceptibility and the development of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arising in susceptible cells can support clonal evolution towards cancer in a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence that environmental exposures influence cancer risk rather than cancer being solely a matter of inherited susceptibility or bad luck.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can contribute to carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a detailed example of cooperating infectious influences.

topics.label: Mechanisms of carcinogen-induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental carcinogens produce potentially mutagenic DNA damage and how biological processing affects that damage.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutational initiation from the promotion of tumour growth through a permissive cellular environment.

topics.label: Developmental and tissue specificity of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how susceptibility to carcinogens depends on the biological context of exposure and consolidate the preceding account of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Evidence linking human cancers to carcinogen exposure
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence from human cancers and populations can identify exposure to carcinogens and support causal attribution.

topics.label: Experimental tests of carcinogenic potential
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how experimental assays assess carcinogenic potential and why their results do not fully capture cancer development in humans.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: The closing draws together the lecture's conclusions about environmental cancer risks and carcinogen assessment within everyday risk–benefit decisions.
